summary: Weekly POC sync focused on unit economics. Reviewed current benchmark numbers, KV/prefix cache impact, and batching tradeoffs. Decided to run an additional 32-batch + cache benchmark and share granular cost model to validate tokens/sec per dollar targets.
topics: next steps for dedicated capacity decision
transcript:
00:00 Maya Patel: ok everyone good to go? hi team, thanks for joining. agenda: quick results review, a few tuning questions, and next steps on cost model
00:13 Olivia Park: yea hi, thanks, we'll jump in. we really want to see if the numbers support a dedicated commit, right. tokens per dollar is our main KPI
00:30 Carlos Mendes: quick context, we reran the seeded workload yesterday with KV cache on and off, batch sizes 8 and 32. duration about 45 minutes including warmup. i have the runs here.
00:45 Ethan Zhou: just flag, our production has a lot of prefix reuse because of templated prompts, so cache hit should be realistic for us.
:58 Priya Kapoor: also want to ensure tail latency doesn't blow up with bigger batches, we need 95th p95 under 400ms for interactive use.
01:10 Carlos Mendes: agree - overall summary: with cache enabled and batch=8 we get about 1.2M tokens per hour on the test shard, cost estimate roughly $X per million tokens (see spreadsheet). with batch=32 and cache enabled throughput increased ~1.6x, tokens/sec up, cost per token dropped accordingly. but p95 moves up ~80-120ms depending on seq len.
01:45 Ethan Zhou: can you translate that into tokens/sec per dollar? that's the metric our CFO cares about.
01:52 Maya Patel: yes - high level: current hosted run (no cache, batch=8) is ~450 tokens/sec per $1. with cache enabled that moves to ~1,100 tokens/sec per $1 because cached prefixes avoid re-compute. with batching 32+cache it's about 1,700 tokens/sec per $1 on this model family. numbers are approximate and depend on quantization and region.
02:20 Olivia Park: interesting, do you have breakdown of where the savings come from? is it compute time saved or memory bandwidth or fewer kv ops?
02:31 Carlos Mendes: mostly compute — the KV cache avoids re-attending to prefix tokens which reduces per-request FLOPs. also less memory shuffle because the batch/kernel amortization improves utilization. there is some serialization overhead at higher batch sizes though.
02:50 Samir Hussain: when you say cache enabled, that's prefix/KV cache at the runtime level not application-side cache, correct?
02:58 Carlos Mendes: correct - it's runtime KV cache. in our POC we enabled prefix reuse across requests; that was safe because requests are deterministic for your template.
03:10 Priya Kapoor: are there accuracy implications for quantized runs? our internal QA is sensitive.
03:18 Carlos Mendes: we ran 8-bit quant for both setups; quality metrics (rouge/bleu-ish proxies we use) were within 1-1.5% relative to float16. if you push to 4-bit q8_0 there can be small diffs; we can show evals.
03:38 Ethan Zhou: can you walk through a sample cost calc?
03:42 Maya Patel: sure - here's a simplified example: assume model cost per GPU-hour = $X, effective tokens/sec observed = T, so tokens per dollar = T / (cost_per_hour / 3600). plug numbers: if T=1200 tokens/sec and cost/hour=6, tokens per dollar ~720k (we include overheads), on batch=32 it becomes ~1.7M tokens per dollar.
04:08 Olivia Park: ok but how sensitive is that to request length distribution? our average is 360 tokens per request, tails up to 2k for a few flows.
04:18 Carlos Mendes: longer average seq length reduces effective tokens/sec because KV servicing and attention scale O(n^2) sometimes; but prefix caching helps a lot when long tails reuse short prefixes. we modeled 3 distributions — median-only, median+long tails, and heavy-tail — numbers vary by ~20-40% between them.
04:45 Priya Kapoor: what about batching latency tradeoff? our app is latency-sensitive for autocomp flows.
04:52 Maya Patel: tradeoff - batching increases throughput and lowers cost per token, but raises p95 and tail. typical approach is hybrid: small batches for low-latency routes and pooled larger batches for background flows. Redwood routing supports per-route policies.
05:10 Ethan Zhou: do you support auto-scaling burst where latency routes get priority?
05:15 Carlos Mendes: yes, request prioritization and lane-based routing. plus fallback to smaller model variant if under high load.
05:24 Olivia Park: any gotchas on the cache side for multi-tenant or privacy?
05:30 Maya Patel: with Dedicated or Private we support tenant isolation; cache keys are scoped to customer and can be encrypted at rest. audit logs show cache hits for compliance.
05:42 Samir Hussain: what's the expected savings percent from caching for our workload? earlier you said ~2-3x tokens/sec improvement; is that realistic?
05:51 Carlos Mendes: for Quantaco templates we saw 2.1-2.6x on the seeded trace given ~35% prefix reuse. if your reuse goes up to 60% savings could be 3x.
06:05 Priya Kapoor: can we get the raw run artifacts? we want to compare with our internal profiler.
06:10 Carlos Mendes: yes i'll dump the benchmark logs, GPU utilization traces, and the run config. will post them in the shared folder.
06:18 Ethan Zhou: about batching, what about micro-batching or accumulation? sometimes you can keep latency but get some aggregation benefits.
06:28 Carlos Mendes: we support micro-batching (gradual accumulation up to X ms) — you can set accumulation windows like 20-50ms to batch quick similar arrivals. it's a nice middle ground.
06:36 Olivia Park: ok, on cost modeling, can you include the cost of storage (KV), network egress, and reserved capacity overheads? our procurement asks for TCO not just per-token compute cost.
06:46 Maya Patel: yes, in the spreadsheet we'll include compute, storage, network egress, and an amortized reserved capacity uplift for Dedicated. we'll show both hosted and dedicated scenarios side-by-side.
07:00 Ethan Zhou: what about orchestration overhead if we use private on-prem? more ops work and license fee, right?
07:07 Maya Patel: Private has a platform fee and potentially higher ops; we list support and platform fees separately in the deck. Dedicated usually hits the sweet spot for you if you want predictable unit economics without full ops burden.
07:20 Olivia Park: can we see a run that mimics our 95th latency distribution?
07:24 Carlos Mendes: yes — action: we'll run a dedicated p95-sensitive profile with batch=8, batch=16, and micro-batching, cache on, and share p50/p95/p99 numbers.
07:36 Priya Kapoor: timing: if those runs look good, we might be ready to talk about a 3-month reserved commit.
07:42 Maya Patel: understood. we'll prioritize the p95 run.
07:48 Samir Hussain: curious on region selection — east vs west for cost delta?
07:53 Carlos Mendes: cost varies 10-20% by cloud region and instance SKU; we'll include region-aware numbers in the sheet.
08:02 Ethan Zhou: any red flags from today's run?
08:05 Carlos Mendes: only thing noticed was one run with degraded nvlink perf causing a 7% dip — that's an infra fluke, not expected at scale. we'll re-run to be safe.
08:16 Olivia Park: ok good. can you also annotate the spreadsheet with assumptions for quantization quality thresholds?
08:21 Maya Patel: yes we'll include a short eval summary with quality deltas for 8-bit and 4-bit profiles.
08:29 Ethan Zhou: last thing — can you show a concrete tokens/sec/$ number per API route? our product has two main routes, small completions and long-document embedding-ish flows.
08:40 Maya Patel: we'll map both routes and provide recommended profiles: small-completions: batch=8+micro-batching, cache on; long-docs: batch=32, cache enabled for prefix reuse, consider quant=8.
08:58 Olivia Park: great. recap and next steps?
09:02 Maya Patel: recap: Carlos will run p95-sensitive benchmarks (batch=8,16,32 + micro-batching) with KV cache and share results by 2025-06-22. I'll share updated pricing / tokens-per-dollar spreadsheet by 2025-06-20. Ethan will upload production traces for reuse analysis by 2025-06-24. We'll schedule dedicated capacity deep dive week of 2025-06-30 if numbers look good.
09:25 Olivia Park: thanks everyone. that works for us.
09:28 Maya Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up in the shared folder. bye.
